content_of_post_to_comment:
Hi all. Well, the penny has finally dropped. It took a while! It has dawned on me that there is no longer anything of value whatsoever on Facebook. The AI slop is out of control, the groups I used to enjoy and find useful are full of bots and trolls, and the hatred for minorities (such as the disabled, of which I am one) is shocking. It really affects my mood. I only really post stuff for attention, which I don't like and is embarrassing to admit to. My posts only garner one or two likes nowadays, which is disappointing. The trouble is, if I stay off FB my best friend says she misses my "pretty posts" (I post art, usually), and she keeps sending me links to FB posts she thinks I ought to see on WhatsApp! Oh well. I think I will unfortunately have to disappoint her, somewhat.

I found out that independent research has estimated that around 10-16% of all accounts on FB are in fact bots. That seems quite a conservative estimate to me. The AI content is getting worse, very quickly. I discovered that around 41% of longer-form FB posts are AI generated, and up to 70% of visual content has been mucked about with by AI. That's phenomenal.

The main problem is that I'm mostly housebound due to health issues, but I do have other interests, such as my book group and Zoom lectures on subjects which interest me, plus a couple of friends I'm in touch with in "real life". I am going to try and strengthen the real life ties, if I can. But staying off FB is the only way to go for my mental health right now.
comment: The bit about your friend missing your pretty posts is tricky, because it sounds like there’s still something meaningful there, just not necessarily in the place those posts live. Maybe you could send her your art directly on WhatsApp instead? You’d keep that connection without having to wade through all the stuff that’s making you miserable.
